outcome: Implemented the PO-requested plain-language confirmation gate ahead of every signature in plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/po-human-approval.mjs: requireExplicitConfirmation() prints the approval kind, the exact candidate commit (plus action subject digest and expiry for -critical), or the intent digest for sign-intent, states that OpenSSL is about to sign with the private key and that this cannot be undone, and requires the literal token "approve"; anything else, including an empty answer, calls fail() before OpenSSL is invoked or any artifact is written. Reading is injectable via dependencies.readConfirmation and otherwise falls back to a synchronous single-line read from fd 0, matching the existing spawnSync-blocking style of this CLI. Wired into approve, approve-critical and sign-intent; approve-all inherits it by recursion (one confirmation per signed proof); setup and the read-only prepare*/verify* branches are deliberately untouched because they sign nothing. Tests: three added/extended cases in po-human-approval.test.mjs covering accept-then-sign with prompt-content assertions (digest named, consequence class named, explicit token required), cancel-on-mismatch and cancel-on-empty, both asserting OpenSSL was never spawned and no proof/signature/intent artifact exists. Reported honestly against its own DoD: node --test po-human-approval.test.mjs 5/5 exit 0 and node --check exit 0, but full verify.mjs exit 1 because plugins/pipeline-core/lib/threat-model-approval-request.test.mjs:73/:76 call approve/approve-all without the new dependency and that file was outside its Forbidden scope; it stopped rather than widen scope. Stopped at the 30-tool-use cap with the work staged but uncommitted, after spending its last call on an inline multi-line -m commit that the shell-grammar guard rejected instead of the scratch-file + -F path its briefing prescribed.
orchestratorCompletion: The Elephant verified the staged diff by reading it rather than trusting the report, then completed the dispatch: injected readConfirmation into the two out-of-scope call sites in threat-model-approval-request.test.mjs with a comment stating why (36/36 pass), documented the gate and the previously undocumented sign-intent subcommand in docs/po-human-approval.md including the German reader aid, and committed. Residual, not fixed here: the confirmation prompt is English-only and does not yet follow runtime.humanFacingLanguage, which the PO's request named explicitly ("je nach Sprachprofil"); recorded as an open item rather than silently treated as delivered.
